<explanation>
Based on the provided file tree and README, I'll explain how to create a comprehensive system design diagram for Visual Pinball, a complex pinball table editor and simulator.

1. Main System Components
The diagram should be organized into these major components:

a. Core Engine Layer
   - Physics Engine (src/physics/)
   - Rendering Engine (src/renderer/)
   - Audio System (src/audio/)
   - Input System (pininput.cpp)

b. Editor Layer
   - Table Editor Components
   - Property Editors (dialogs/Properties/)
   - Live UI System (LiveUI.cpp)
   - Material System (Material.h)

c. Scripting System
   - VBScript Integration (scripts/)
   - Event System (eventproxy.cpp)

d. Asset Management
   - Mesh Management (src/meshes/)
   - Texture Management (src/renderer/TextureManager)
   - Sound Management (src/audio/)

2. Component Relationships

Draw the following connections:

a. Data Flow
   - Table Editor → Core Engine
   - Physics Engine → Rendering Engine
   - Input System → Physics Engine
   - Scripting System → All Components

b. Asset Pipeline
   - Mesh Files → Mesh Management → Rendering Engine
   - Texture Files → Texture Management → Rendering Engine
   - Sound Files → Audio System

3. External Integrations

Include these external systems:
   - DirectX/OpenGL Rendering
   - Visual PinMAME Integration
   - VR/HMD Support
   - BAM Head Tracking
   - Touch/Tablet Input

4. Specific Implementation Details

Use color coding to distinguish:
   - Blue: Core Engine Components
   - Green: Editor Components
   - Yellow: Scripting System
   - Orange: Asset Management
   - Purple: External Integrations

5. Component Details

For each major component, show:
   - Input/Output relationships
   - Key classes and their relationships
   - Resource flow
   - Event handling paths

6. Technical Specifications

Include these elements:
   - Supported rendering backends (DirectX/OpenGL)
   - Physics simulation components
   - Input handling systems
   - VR/3D display support

7. Architecture Patterns

Highlight these patterns:
   - Model-View-Controller for the editor
   - Component-based architecture for game objects
   - Event-driven architecture for scripting
   - Resource management system

The diagram should be layered from top to bottom:
1. User Interface Layer (Editor, Properties, Live UI)
2. Scripting Layer (VBScript, Events)
3. Core Systems Layer (Physics, Rendering, Audio)
4. Platform Integration Layer (DirectX/OpenGL, Input Devices)

Use clear, directional arrows to show data flow and dependencies between components. Include a legend explaining all symbols and color codes used in the diagram.

This architecture reflects both the real-time simulation aspects of the pinball engine and the creative tools needed for table editing, while maintaining extensibility through scripting and external device support.
